identity.title: ALMA observations of A0620-00: fresh clues on the nature of quiescent black hole X-ray binary jets
identity.journal: Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society

paper_type_evidence.quote: We report on ALMA continuum observations of the black hole X-ray binary A0620–00, at an X-ray luminosity nine orders of magnitude sub-Eddington.

evidence.quote: At $L_{\rm X}$$\simeq 10^{-9}$ $L_{\rm Edd}$, and $1.06\pm0.12$ kpc distance (cite: cantrell10)
At $L_{\rm X}$$\simeq 10^{-9}$ $L_{\rm Edd}$, and $1.06\pm0.12$ kpc distance (cite: cantrell10)

question.value: Is the sub-mm/mm spectrum of the quiescent black hole X-ray binary A0620-00 optically thin, or is its jet emission highly variable, and what does this imply for the jet spectral extent?

evidence.quote: These results suggest either an optically thin sub-mm synchrotron spectrum, or highly variable sub-mm jet emission on month timescales.
were taken as part of project 2016.1.00773.S (P.I. Gallo).

bands.value: Band 3 (98 GHz) and Band 6 (233 GHz) continuum

evidence.quote: Continuum observations in Band 3 at 98 GHz and Band 6 at 233 GHz were taken

baselines.value: Band 3: 15-1039 m (46 antennas); Band 6: 15-491 m (48 antennas)

evidence.quote: with 46 antennas, with baselines spanning the range 15 m to 1039 m
For the Band 6 data the synthesized beam is $0.86\ensuremath{''} \times 0.77\ensuremath{''}$ at a position angle of $-71.3\ensuremath{^\circ}$
with an rms noise of $8.2~\mu{\rm Jy~beam}^{-1}$
for 2.15 hr

observing_dates.value: Band 3: 12 and 14 Nov 2016; Band 6: 20 and 21 Dec 2016

evidence.quote: The Band 6 data were taken on the 20th and 21st December 2016
(P.I. Gallo)

provided.value: X-band 8-12 GHz radio flux densities, 13 observations Sep 2017-Jan 2018 (program 17B-233)

evidence.quote: We measured flux densities of $12.9\pm1.5$ and $14.2 \pm 1.8$ $\mu$Jy bm$^{-1}$ at 8.9 and 10.8 GHz, respectively.

provided.value: optical/NIR photometry, simultaneous with ALMA Band 6

evidence.quote: A0620–00 is routinely monitored at optical and near-IR (NIR) frequencies with the dual-channel imager ANDICAM on the SMARTS 1.3 m telescope

what.value: Earlier SEDs (2003-2005 VLA, SMARTS, Chandra, Spitzer; 2013 VLA and SMARTS) for comparison

evidence.quote: red open triangles correspond to the 2003-2005 campaign reported by Gallo et al. (2007; VLA, SMARTS and *Chandra*)

external_data_from_literature.citation: Gallo et al. 2007; Dincer et al. 2018 (cite: dincer18); Muno (cite: muno)

evidence.quote: the color excess $E(B-V)=0.30\pm 0.05$ (Cantrell et al. 2010)

pipeline_or_manual.value: ALMA pipeline script provided by ALMA staff, run in CASA

evidence.quote: The data were calibrated using $\texttt{CASA}$ (cite: McMullin_ea_2007) using the pipeline script provided by ALMA staff.
the quasars J0750+1231 and J0641-0320 were used for flux and phase calibration, respectively
Absolute flux calibration adds a systematic uncertainties of 5 per cent for Band 3 and 10 per cent for Band 6
there was insufficient signal to perform self-calibration
The data were imaged using natural weighting to maximize sensitivity
achieving a beam size of $1.25\ensuremath{''} \times 1.10\ensuremath{''}$
a root mean square (rms) noise of $6.9~\mu{\rm Jy~beam}^{-1}$

what.value: SMARTS data reduction follows standard procedures

evidence.quote: Data presented here were reduced following standard procedures described in (cite: dincer18)

unstated_but_needed: CASA version used for ALMA pipeline
Image size, cell size, and tclean parameters
Whether archive pipeline products were used as delivered

method.value: ALMA pipeline calibration, no self-cal, natural-weighted imaging

evidence.quote: The data were imaged using natural weighting to maximize sensitivity

validation.value: Phase decorrelation test: reran pipeline treating three phase-calibrator scans as target; peak within 5%

evidence.quote: This confirms that phase decorrelation as a function of time was $<$5 per cent during the Band 6 observations.

method.value: Fit 2D Gaussian with beam properties to continuum images, flux and position free

evidence.quote: The integrated flux densities were measured by fitting a 2D Gaussian with the same properties as the synthesized beam to the continuum images

fitting.value: Affine-invariant MCMC ensemble sampler; 16th-84th percentiles for uncertainty

evidence.quote: Posterior distributions were sampled using an affine invariant Markov chain Monte Carlo ensemble sampler

analysis_steps.goal: compute spectral index and compare with multiwavelength SEDs

method.value: Two-point 98-233 GHz index; compare with VLA, SMARTS and earlier campaigns

evidence.quote: with $\alpha={-0.56\pm 0.47}$ (3$\sigma$ C.L.) over the 98–233 GHz frequency interval
the color excess $E(B-V)=0.30\pm 0.05$ (Cantrell et al. 2010)

software.name: CASA
software.version: v5.1.1 for VLA; ALMA version not stated

used_for.value: ALMA pipeline calibration and VLA processing

evidence.quote: Data were processed using CASA v5.1.1
`emcee` (cite: Foreman-Mackey_ea_2013)
yielding a robust detection in Band 3, at $44 \pm 7~\mu{\rm Jy}$
a marginally significant detection in band 6, at $20 \pm 8~\mu{\rm Jy}$

findings_qualitative.value: At ALMA epochs A0620-00 was less active in optical-IR than during earlier campaigns suggesting a flat-spectrum jet

evidence.quote: A0620–00 was somewhat less active than during other published multi-wavelength campaigns

claims.hypothesis: Is the mm spectrum optically thin or is the jet variable?
claims.experiment: Dual-band ALMA continuum 40 days apart with SMARTS and VLA context
claims.result: 44±7 uJy at 98 GHz, 20±8 uJy at 233 GHz
claims.finding: Either an optically thin spectrum or factor >=2 variability over a month; variability more likely

evidence.quote: it is also possible – and arguably more likely – that the measured values indicate a factor $\lower.5ex\hbox{$\; \buildrel > \over \sim \;$}2$ variability

claims.hypothesis: Do BH XRB jets vary strongly across Eddington ratios?
claims.experiment: Combine ALMA with results from V404 Cyg and Cyg X-1

evidence.quote: jets from black hole X-ray binaries exhibit a high level of variability across a wide spectrum of Eddington ratios.

limitations_admitted.value: Observations not simultaneous across radio, mm and IR; no firm conclusions

evidence.quote: no firm conclusions can be drawn based upon on the dual band ALMA observations

referee_caveats_inferred: Non-simultaneous Band 3 and 6 limits spectral inference

reproducibility.score_reason: Public project code and simple recipe, but imaging and fit details are sparse.
reproducibility.rediscovery_reason: Recipe incomplete and the main results are two faint flux densities with limited detail.

companion_papers.why: previous SED campaign and SMARTS reduction
